newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks close down after Dow dips.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks close down after Dow dips.

text.p: SPI Futures 2394 -30 US 30yr 6.94 +0.05
10yrbond futs 92.460 -0.070 Gold NY 356.45 Lon fix 353.10
*Stocks end lower after Dow continues downtrend. Golds give only good news. Volume 347.20 million, value A$723.95 million, 1,115 stocks traded, 310 steady, 307 up, 498 down.
The Australian share market closed lower on Tuesday after the Dow continued its downtrend.
The only local bright spot was a gold sector that received a pick-me-up from a firmer bullion price in offshore markets.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was down 18.8 points at 2,404.2.
March share price index futures were 30 points lower at 2,394, a 10.2 point discount to the index.
Resuming from a holiday long weekend, the local market played catchup to two days of Wall Street weakness and losses were widely spread.
"It is the Dow hanging over our heads again," said senior dealer at Nevitts Ltd, Jim Tredenick, adding that heavier losses would not have surprised.
"I thought it might have come off a bit more but overall our market hasn't done too badly."

Other players agreed, noting that the March SPI futures contract had settled at a discount to the benchmark All Ordinaries index, with traders cautious ahead of U.S. wages data due later on Tuesday and local inflation data due Wednesaday.
"It's been a Dow-driven day," said a Sydney broker.
"The SPI seems set at a discount as traders short or cut positions ahead of the U.S. tonight."
In the golds, Acacia Resources, up 2.8 percent to A$2.19, Plutonic also up 2.8 percent to A$5.15, and Normandy Mining, whose scrip added 2.5 percent to A$1.63, were the pick.
Elsewhere, shares in metals recycler Simsmetal lost 29 cents to close at A$6.99 after posting a 43 percent lower first half net profit of A$$14.07 million.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade was moderate but futures trade was active as players shuffled positions ahead of both US and local economic data. Total options traded 36,718 (30,095) Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 10,474 (8,447)

In other local markets, the Australian dollar remained locked in a tight, tense standoff with its U.S. counterpart, but did make up ground on most crosses with scant reaction to the government's mid-year economic review in which forecasts for 1996/97 inflation were lowered while GDP growth remained the same at 3.5 percent. Analysts saw little in the review to change thinking on interest rates, and so the dollar.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the local dollar was idling at US$0.7731/36 from an early US$0.7721/26 and a US$0.7730/35 here late Friday.
Australian bonds finished down but were bouyant in late trade, most notably at short end, after the release of the mid-year budget review.
The market is now awaiting on U.S. employment cost index later on Tuesday and local December quarter CPI data on Wednesday.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.45 percent, up 0.07 from Friday's 7.38 percent.
